s0003.literal: Du Sengming; Zhou Wenyu, son Bao'an; Hou Andu
s0003.idiomatic: Du Sengming; Zhou Wenyu, son Bao'an; Hou Andu

s0004.literal: Du Sengming, style Hongzhao, was a native of Linze in Guangling.
s0004.idiomatic: Du Sengming, styled Hongzhao, came from Linze in Guangling.

s0005.literal: Small in stature, yet his daring surpassed other men; he had courage and strength and was skilled in riding and archery.
s0005.idiomatic: He was small in stature, yet his daring surpassed other men; he had courage and strength and fought well from horseback.

s0006.literal: In the Datong era of Liang, Lu Anxing was superintendent of the Southern River in Guangzhou; Sengming, his elder brother Tianhe, and Zhou Wenyu were all recommended by Anxing and asked to go with him.
s0006.idiomatic: In Liang's Datong era Lu Anxing was superintendent of Guangzhou's Southern River. Sengming, his elder brother Tianhe, and Zhou Wenyu were all brought forward by Anxing and went with him.

s0007.literal: He repeatedly campaigned against the Li and Liao with merit and was made assistant defender of Xinzhou.
s0007.idiomatic: On repeated campaigns against the Li and Liao he earned merit and was made assistant defender of Xinzhou.

s0008.literal: Tianhe also had ability and took part in the campaigns.
s0008.idiomatic: Tianhe too had talent and shared in the fighting.

s0009.literal: When Anxing died, Sengming again served as deputy to his son Zixiong.
s0009.idiomatic: When Anxing died, Sengming again served under his son Zixiong.

s0010.literal: When the powerful local man Li Ben of Jiaozhou rebelled, drove out Inspector Xiao Zi, and Zi fled to Guangzhou, the court sent Zixiong and Sun Tong, inspector of Gaozhou, to campaign against Ben.
s0010.idiomatic: When Li Ben, a powerful man of Jiaozhou, rebelled and drove out Inspector Xiao Zi, who fled to Guangzhou, the court sent Zixiong and Sun Tong of Gaozhou against him.

s0011.literal: Spring grass was already growing and miasma rising; Zixiong asked to wait until autumn to attack, but Xiao Mo, Prince of Xinyu and inspector of Guangzhou, would not listen, and Xiao Zi again pressed them, so Zixiong and the others had no choice but to march.
s0011.idiomatic: Spring grass was up and miasma rising. Zixiong asked to wait for autumn, but Prince Xinyu Xiao Mo, inspector of Guangzhou, refused, and Xiao Zi pressed again, so they marched against their will.

s0012.literal: Reaching Hepu, six or seven in ten died; the troops feared the corvée and scattered; they could not be stopped, and he led the remnant back.
s0012.idiomatic: At Hepu six or seven in ten died. The troops feared the levy and broke; nothing could hold them, and he led the remnant home.

s0013.literal: Xiao Zi reported that Zixiong and Tong had dealings with the bandits and lingered without advancing; Emperor Wu of Liang had them imprisoned at Guangzhou and put to death.
s0013.idiomatic: Xiao Zi reported that Zixiong and Tong trafficked with the rebels and would not advance. Emperor Wu of Liang had them imprisoned at Guangzhou and put to death.

s0014.literal: Zixiong's younger cousin Zilue and Zilie were bold and chivalrous; their families were in the Southern River region.
s0014.idiomatic: Zixiong's cousins Zilue and Zilie were bold and chivalrous men; their kin still lived in the Southern River country.

s0015.literal: Tianhe plotted with the troops, saying: "Master Lu treated us generously for generations; now he has been killed unjustly and we cannot repay him—this is not the act of a true man.
s0015.idiomatic: Tianhe took counsel with the troops: "The Lu house treated us well for generations; now they have been killed unjustly and we cannot repay them—what man would bear this?

s0016.literal: My brother Sengming is a match for ten thousand men; if we surround the prefectural city and summon the people, who would not follow?
s0016.idiomatic: My brother Sengming is worth ten thousand men. Ring the prefectural city and call the people—who would not answer?

s0017.literal: When the city falls, behead the two marquises to avenge Sun and Lu, then wait for the court envoy, bind our hands, and go to the Minister of Justice—death is better than life.
s0017.idiomatic: When the walls fall, strike off the two marquises for Sun and Lu, then wait for the court envoy, go bound to the Minister of Justice, and die rather than live on in shame.

s0018.literal: Even if we do not succeed, we shall have no regret."
s0018.idiomatic: Even if we fail, we shall have no regret."

s0019.literal: The troops all cried out in zeal: "That is our wish; we await only your command."
s0019.idiomatic: The troops answered hotly: "That is our wish; command us as you will."

s0020.literal: Thereupon, with Zhou Wenyu and others, he led the troops in alliance, set up Zixiong's cousin Zilue as leader, and attacked Inspector Xiao Ying.
s0020.idiomatic: Then he and Zhou Wenyu and others swore the troops together, set up Zilue, Zixiong's cousin, as leader, and marched on Inspector Xiao Ying.

s0021.literal: Zilue held the south of the city, Tianhe the north; Sengming and Wenyu held east and west; officials and people all responded; within a day troops reached tens of thousands.
s0021.idiomatic: Zilue held the south gate, Tianhe the north; Sengming and Wenyu took east and west. Officials and commoners rose with them, and in a single day troops numbered in the tens of thousands.

s0022.literal: The Founder was then at Gaoyao; hearing of the rising, he led troops to attack, routed them utterly, killed Tianhe, and took Sengming and Wenyu alive; the Founder released them and made them his commanders.
s0022.idiomatic: The Founder was at Gaoyao. Hearing of the revolt, he marched, broke them completely, killed Tianhe, and took Sengming and Wenyu alive. He freed them and kept them as his commanders.

s0023.literal: When the Founder campaigned in Jiaozhi and against Yuan Jingzhong, Sengming and Wenyu both had merit.
s0023.idiomatic: On the Founder's campaigns in Jiaozhi and against Yuan Jingzhong, Sengming and Wenyu both won honor.

s0024.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion they both followed the Founder to relieve the capital.
s0024.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion they both followed the Founder to relieve the capital.

s0025.literal: When the Founder defeated Lan Yu at Shixing, Sengming was vanguard, took Yu prisoner, and beheaded him.
s0025.idiomatic: When the Founder broke Lan Yu at Shixing, Sengming led the van, seized Yu, and struck off his head.

s0026.literal: Again, fighting Cai Luyang at Nanye, Sengming's horse was wounded; the Founder galloped to save him and gave him his own mount; Sengming remounted and with several dozen men pressed on again; the troops all scattered before him, and pressing the advantage he routed Luyang utterly.
s0026.idiomatic: Fighting Cai Luyang at Nanye, Sengming's horse was wounded. The Founder galloped to his aid and gave him his own mount. Sengming charged again with a few dozen men; the troops broke before him, and he drove Luyang to utter defeat.

s0027.literal: Li Qianshi, inspector of Gaozhou, again held Daqiang, entered Ganshi, and pressed the Founder; the Founder sent Zhou Wenyu as vanguard with Sengming to drive him off.
s0027.idiomatic: Li Qianshi of Gaozhou again held Daqiang, entered Ganshi, and threatened the Founder. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyu ahead with Sengming and drove him back.

s0028.literal: Qianshi and Liu Xiaoshang of Ningdu joined forces to strike at Nankang; the Founder again ordered Sengming with Wenyu and others to resist; they fought for more than a hundred days straight and at last took Qianshi and sent him to the Founder's camp.
s0028.idiomatic: Qianshi and Liu Xiaoshang of Ningdu meant to strike Nankang together. The Founder sent Sengming and Wenyu to hold them; for more than a hundred days they fought without rest, took Qianshi at last, and sent him to the Founder's camp.

s0029.literal: When the Founder descended on Nankang he left Sengming at Xichang to oversee military affairs in Ancheng and Luling commanderies.
s0029.idiomatic: When the Founder took Nankang he left Sengming at Xichang to command Ancheng and Luling.

s0030.literal: Emperor Yuan, acting on provisional authority, granted him credential staff, general who clears the wilds, inspector of Xinzhou, and enfeoffment as Viscount of Linjiang with a fief of three hundred households.
s0030.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang, on provisional commission, made him credential-bearer, general who clears the wilds, inspector of Xinzhou, and Viscount of Linjiang with three hundred households.

s0031.literal: Zhou Wenyu, style Jingde, was a native of Yangxian in Yixing.
s0031.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyu, styled Jingde, came from Yangxian in Yixing.

s0032.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he originally lived in Shouchang county in Xin'an; his surname was Xiang and his name Mengnu.
s0032.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he had lived in Shouchang in Xin'an; his family name was Xiang and his childhood name Mengnu.

s0033.literal: At eleven he could swim back and forth in the water for several li and leap five or six chi; playing with village boys, none could match him.
s0033.idiomatic: At eleven he could swim several li back and forth and leap five or six chi high. Among village boys at play, none could match him.

s0034.literal: Zhou Hui of Yixing was garrison chief at Shouchang Ford; seeing him, he marveled and summoned him to talk.
s0034.idiomatic: Zhou Hui of Yixing held the ford at Shouchang. Struck by the boy, he called him to speak.

s0035.literal: Wenyu answered: "My mother is old, our house is poor, my elder brother and sisters are all grown, and we are crushed by taxes and corvée."
s0035.idiomatic: Wenyu said, "Mother is old, the house is poor, brother and sisters are grown, and taxes and corvée crush us."

s0036.literal: Hui pitied him, followed Wenyu home, and asked his mother to let him adopt Wenyu as his son; the mother consented.
s0036.idiomatic: Hui was moved, went to his home, and asked his mother to let him adopt the boy; she agreed.

s0037.literal: When Hui's term ended he returned to the capital with Wenyu, saw Zhou She, director of the heir apparent's household, and asked that a formal name be given; She thereupon named him Wenyu, style Jingde.
s0037.idiomatic: When Hui's term ended he took Wenyu to the capital, saw Zhou She of the heir's household, and asked a formal name. She named him Wenyu and styled him Jingde.

s0038.literal: He ordered his nephew Hongrang to teach him writing and reckoning.
s0038.idiomatic: He set his nephew Hongrang to teach him letters and accounts.

s0039.literal: Hongrang was skilled in clerical script and copied Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning and ancient poems to give Wenyu; Wenyu did not look at them and said to Hongrang: "Who can learn this? To win wealth and rank you need only a great spear."
s0039.idiomatic: Hongrang wrote clerical script well and copied Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning and old poems for him. Wenyu never read them and told Hongrang, "Who learns such things? Wealth and rank come from a great spear alone."

s0040.literal: Hongrang admired him and taught him riding and archery; Wenyu was greatly pleased.
s0040.idiomatic: Hongrang admired his spirit and taught him riding and archery; Wenyu rejoiced.

s0041.literal: Inspector of Sizhou Chen Qingzhi was from the same commandery as Hui and on good terms with him; he recommended Hui as commander of the vanguard army.
s0041.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi, inspector of Sizhou, was Hui's countryman and friend and had him made commander of the vanguard.

s0042.literal: Qingzhi sent Hui with five hundred men to Xincai and Xuanhuo to comfort the White Water Man; the Man plotted to seize Hui and deliver him to Wei; the plot was discovered, and Hui with Wenyu resisted.
s0042.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Hui with five hundred men to Xincai and Xuanhuo to comfort the White Water Man. The Man plotted to seize Hui for Wei; the plot came out, and Hui and Wenyu fought them off.

s0043.literal: The bandits were very strong; in one day they fought several dozen engagements; Wenyu led the van and broke the line, his courage foremost in the army.
s0043.idiomatic: The rebels were fierce; in a single day they fought dozens of times. Wenyu led the van and broke the array, bravest in the host.

s0044.literal: Hui died in battle; Wenyu galloped to take his corpse, and the bandits did not dare press him.
s0044.idiomatic: Hui fell on the field. Wenyu galloped in for his body, and the rebels did not dare close.

s0045.idiomatic: At evening both sides drew off.

s0046.literal: Wenyu bore nine wounds; when they healed he asked leave to bury Hui; Qingzhi admired his constancy, gave him rich gifts, and sent him away.
s0046.idiomatic: Wenyu took nine wounds. When they healed he begged leave to bury Hui. Qingzhi honored his loyalty, gave him rich gifts, and let him go.

s0047.literal: After the burial Lu Anxing became superintendent of the Southern River and recommended Wenyu to go with him.
s0047.idiomatic: After the rites Lu Anxing became superintendent of the Southern River and had Wenyu go with him.

s0048.literal: On repeated campaigns against the Li and Liao he had merit wherever he went and was made magistrate of Nanhai.
s0048.idiomatic: On repeated campaigns against the Li and Liao he won merit everywhere and was made magistrate of Nanhai.

s0049.literal: After Anxing's death Wenyu with Du Sengming attacked Guangzhou, was defeated by the Founder, and the Founder pardoned him—the account is in Sengming's biography.
s0049.idiomatic: After Anxing died Wenyu and Du Sengming attacked Guangzhou, were beaten by the Founder, and pardoned—the tale is told in Sengming's biography.

s0050.literal: Later Supervisor of the Province Wang Li made Wenyu chief
s0050.idiomatic: Later Supervisor Wang Li made Wenyu chief

s0052.literal: , Editorial footnote marker 3. and deeply trusted him.

s0053.literal: When Li was replaced Wenyu wished to go downriver with him; reaching Dayu Ridge he consulted a diviner, who said: "If you go north you will be no more than a magistrate; if you go south you will become a marquis or duke."
s0053.idiomatic: When Li was replaced Wenyu meant to go down with him. At Dayu Ridge he asked a diviner, who said, "Go north and you will be no more than a magistrate; go south and you will be marquis or duke."

s0054.literal: Wenyu said: "Enough money is enough—who looks to be marquis or duke?"
s0054.idiomatic: Wenyu said, "Enough silver is enough—who dreams of marquis or duke?"

s0055.literal: The diviner also said: "You will presently gain two thousand taels of silver at a stroke; if you do not believe it, take this as proof."
s0055.idiomatic: The diviner added, "You will soon win two thousand taels of silver at a throw. If you doubt it, watch for this sign."

s0056.literal: That evening he lodged at an inn; a merchant asked to gamble with Wenyu; Wenyu won and took two thousand taels of silver.
s0056.idiomatic: That night at an inn a merchant asked to gamble. Wenyu won two thousand taels.

s0057.literal: Next morning he took leave of Li; Li asked the reason; Wenyu told him, and Li then sent him on.
s0057.idiomatic: At dawn he bade Li farewell. Li asked why; Wenyu told him, and Li sent him south.

s0058.literal: The Founder was at Gaoyao; hearing of his return he was greatly pleased, sent men to welcome him, rewarded him richly, and assigned men from his own command.
s0058.idiomatic: The Founder was at Gaoyao. Hearing Wenyu had returned, he rejoiced, sent men to meet him, gave rich rewards, and allotted troops from his own command.

s0059.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing, Wenyu with Du Sengming were vanguard, took Lan Yu, relieved Ouyang Yi, and in each had merit.
s0059.idiomatic: On the Founder's campaign against Hou Jing, Wenyu and Du Sengming led the van, took Lan Yu, relieved Ouyang Yi, and won merit in every fight.

s0060.literal: When the Founder broke Cai Luyang at Nanye, Wenyu was surrounded by Luyang, several rings deep on every side, arrows and stones raining; his horse died; Wenyu fought with his right hand and with his left unbuckled the saddle, broke out of the encirclement, joined Du Sengming and the others, joined strength again, and at last routed them utterly.
s0060.idiomatic: When the Founder broke Cai Luyang at Nanye, Wenyu was ringed by Luyang, arrows and stones like rain, his horse killed. He fought with his right hand, unbuckled the saddle with his left, burst the ring, found Sengming and the rest, charged again together, and routed Luyang utterly.

s0061.literal: The Founder then memorialized that Wenyu be made staff marshal of the headquarters.
s0061.idiomatic: The Founder then had Wenyu made staff marshal of his headquarters.

s0062.literal: When Li Qianshi held Daqiang he sent his general Du Pinglu into Ganshi to build a fort at Yuliang; the Founder ordered Wenyu to attack; Pinglu abandoned the fort and fled, and Wenyu took it.
s0062.idiomatic: Li Qianshi held Daqiang and sent Du Pinglu into Ganshi to build at Yuliang. The Founder ordered Wenyu against him. Pinglu fled the fort and Wenyu seized it.

s0063.literal: Qianshi heard Pinglu had been beaten, left the old and weak at Daqiang, chose picked troops to lead himself, and attacked Wenyu; his edge was very sharp and the soldiers feared him.
s0063.idiomatic: Hearing Pinglu was beaten, Qianshi left the weak at Daqiang, chose elite troops, and led them against Wenyu himself. His spear was sharp and the army feared him.

s0064.literal: Wenyu fought him; Qianshi gradually gave ground; the stalemate was not broken; the Founder sent Du Sengming to aid him; he separately broke Qianshi's river army; Qianshi's troops collapsed; he did not dare pass Daqiang and fled straight to Xingan.
s0064.idiomatic: Wenyu met him in battle. Qianshi slowly gave way; the fight hung deadlocked until the Founder sent Du Sengming. Sengming broke Qianshi's fleet apart; Qianshi's troops collapsed, he dared not pass Daqiang, and fled to Xingan.

s0065.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang granted Wenyu credential staff, stern-faith general, and inspector of Yizhou.
s0065.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang gave Wenyu credential staff, stern-faith general, and inspector of Yizhou.

s0066.literal: Qianshi again plotted with Liu Xiaoshang to resist the army of righteousness; the Founder sent Wenyu with Hou Andu, Du Sengming, Xu Du, and Du Ling to build a fort at Baikou to resist them.
s0066.idiomatic: Qianshi again joined Liu Xiaoshang to resist the loyal army. The Founder sent Wenyu with Hou Andu, Du Sengming, Xu Du, and Du Ling to fortify Baikou.

s0067.literal: Wenyu went out repeatedly to fight and at last took Qianshi prisoner.
s0067.idiomatic: Wenyu sallied again and again and at last took Qianshi.

s0068.literal: The Founder set out from Nankang and sent Wenyu with five thousand men to open the Tong River route.
s0068.idiomatic: The Founder marched from Nankang and sent Wenyu with five thousand men to open the Tong River road.

s0069.literal: Hou Jing's general Wang Bichou held Yuzhang; Wenyu drove him off and then held the city.
s0069.idiomatic: Hou Jing's general Wang Bichou held Yuzhang. Wenyu drove him off and took the city.

s0070.literal: For accumulated merit he was made general of roaming cavalry, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongqian with a fief of five hundred households.
s0070.idiomatic: For repeated honors he was made general of roaming cavalry and supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffed Marquis of Dongqian with five hundred households.

s0071.literal: When the Founder's army reached Baimao Bay he ordered Wenyu and Du Sengming always to serve as army point; they pacified Nanling, Que tou, and other cities.
s0071.idiomatic: At Baimao Bay the Founder set Wenyu and Du Sengming always at the army's point and they took Nanling, Que tou, and other towns.

s0072.literal: Reaching Gushu he fought Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian and broke him.
s0072.idiomatic: At Gushu he fought Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian and broke him.

s0073.literal: When Jing was pacified he was made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, his enfeoffment changed to Marquis of Nanyi with a fief of one thousand households, and he was appointed administrator of Xinyi.
s0073.idiomatic: When Jing fell he was made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, raised to Marquis of Nanyi with one thousand households, and made administrator of Xinyi.

s0074.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to administrator of Nandanyang, Lanling, and Jinling, wise martial general, and scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
s0074.idiomatic: He rose through administrator of Nandanyang, Lanling, and Jinling to wise-martial general and scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

s0075.literal: When the Founder executed Wang Sengbian he ordered Wenyu to command the army and join Emperor Wen at Wuxing to besiege Du Kan and take him.
s0075.idiomatic: When the Founder killed Wang Sengbian he sent Wenyu to command troops and join Emperor Wen at Wuxing, besiege Du Kan, and take him.

s0076.literal: He also crossed the river in a surprise attack on Kuaiji Administrator Zhang Biao and took the commandery city.
s0076.idiomatic: He crossed the river in a surprise stroke on Zhang Biao, administrator of Kuaiji, and seized the commandery seat.

s0077.literal: When Emperor Wen was attacked by Biao, Wenyu was then encamped at Xiangyan Temple north of the city; Emperor Wen went by night to join him, and together they built a palisade.
s0077.idiomatic: When Biao struck Emperor Wen, Wenyu lay at Xiangyan Temple north of the city. Emperor Wen came by night; together they threw up a palisade.

s0078.literal: Before long Biao attacked again; Wenyu fought with all his strength; Biao could not take him and was at last broken and pacified.
s0078.idiomatic: Soon Biao attacked again. Wenyu fought with everything he had; Biao could not break him and was destroyed at last.

s0079.literal: The Founder, because Hou Tian held

s0081.literal: [Jiang] province, Editorial footnote marker 4. ordered Wenyu to campaign against him and at the same time made him commander-in-chief of the military affairs of South Yuzhou
s0081.idiomatic: Jiang province [4], the Founder ordered Wenyu against him and made him commander-in-chief of South Yuzhou

s0083.literal: , martial prestige general, and inspector of South Yuzhou, Editorial footnote marker 5. and led troops in a surprise attack on Xuncheng.
s0083.idiomatic: [5], martial-prestige general and inspector of South Yuzhou, and sent him to storm Xuncheng.

s0084.literal: He did not take it; Xu Siwei brought Qi invaders across the river and held Wuhu; an edict recalled Wenyu to the capital.
s0084.idiomatic: Xuncheng did not fall. Xu Siwei brought Qi troops across the Yangzi and held Wuhu; an edict recalled Wenyu to the capital.

s0085.literal: Siwei and the others lined ships from Qingdun to Qiji to cut Wenyu's line of retreat.
s0085.idiomatic: Siwei ranged ships from Qingdun to Qiji to sever Wenyu's retreat.

s0086.literal: At evening Wenyu drummed and set out shouting; Siwei and the others could not stop him.
s0086.idiomatic: At dusk Wenyu beat the drums and broke out shouting. Siwei could not hold him.

s0087.literal: At dawn he turned and attacked Siwei; Siwei's fierce general Bao Peng alone with a small ship brought up the rear; Wenyu boarded a single skiff to fight, leaped into Peng's ship, beheaded Peng, and towed the ship back.
s0087.idiomatic: At dawn he turned on Siwei. Siwei's champion Bao Peng alone brought up the rear in a small craft. Wenyu took a single skiff, leaped aboard, killed Peng, and towed the ship away.

s0088.literal: The rebel troops were greatly shaken; they therefore left their ships at Wuhu and went up from Danyang on foot.
s0088.idiomatic: The rebel host was shaken. They left their ships at Wuhu and marched up from Danyang on foot.

s0089.literal: The Founder was then resisting Siwei at Baicheng and happened to join Wenyu in great force.
s0089.idiomatic: The Founder was holding Siwei at Baicheng and met Wenyu in full strength.

s0090.literal: About to give battle, the wind was fierce; the Founder said: "Troops do not go against the wind."
s0090.idiomatic: As battle neared the wind blew hard. The Founder said, "Soldiers do not fight against the wind."

s0091.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6. Wenyu said: "The matter is urgent—we must decide; what use is the old rule?"
s0091.idiomatic: [6] Wenyu said, "This is urgent—we must decide now. What use is the old rule?"

s0092.literal: He drew his spear, mounted, and galloped forward; Editorial footnote marker 7. the army followed; the wind soon shifted too, and several hundred were killed and wounded.
s0092.idiomatic: He seized his spear, mounted, and charged. [7] The army followed; the wind shifted; several hundred fell killed or wounded.

s0093.literal: Siwei and the others moved camp to Mofu Mountain; Editorial footnote marker 8. Wenyu shifted his encampment to face them.
s0093.idiomatic: Siwei moved camp to Mofu Mountain. [8] Wenyu shifted to face him.

s0094.literal: In repeated fighting his merit was foremost; he was advanced to general who pacifies the west and raised to Duke of Shouchang, and was also given one set of pipes and drums.
s0094.idiomatic: In repeated fighting his merit stood first. He was made general who pacifies the west, raised to Duke of Shouchang, and given pipes and drums.

s0095.literal: Xiao Bo, inspector of Guangzhou, raised troops and crossed the ranges; an edict ordered Wenyu to command the army to campaign against him.
s0095.idiomatic: Xiao Bo, inspector of Guangzhou, rose and crossed the mountains. An edict set Wenyu at the head of the army against him.

s0096.literal: At that time the cave lord of Xinwu Yu Xiaoding
s0096.idiomatic: Then Yu Xiaoding, cave lord of Xinwu,

s0098.literal: [raised] troops in response to Bo, Editorial footnote marker 9. sent his younger brother Xiaoxun to hold the commandery city, and himself came out to Yuzhang and held Shitou.
s0098.idiomatic: [9] rose for Bo, sent his brother Xiaoxun to hold the commandery seat, and himself marched to Yuzhang and seized Shitou.

s0099.literal: Bo sent his son Zi with troops to join Xiaoding and also sent his separate general Ouyang Yi to encamp at Kuzhu Ford and Fu Tai to hold Yankou city, Editorial footnote marker 10. to resist the government army.
s0099.idiomatic: Bo sent his son Zi to join Xiaoding and his generals Ouyang Yi to Kuzhu Ford and Fu Tai to Yankou [10] to block the loyal army.

s0100.literal: The government army had few ships; Xiaoding had three hundred skiffs and more than a hundred war vessels upstream at Shanglao; Editorial footnote marker 11. Wenyu sent commanders Jiao Songdu and Yang Jian with a hidden force to strike them, took them all, and still built a palisade at Yuzhang.
s0100.idiomatic: The loyal army had few ships. Xiaoding kept three hundred skiffs and more than a hundred war craft at Shanglao. [11] Wenyu sent Jiao Songdu and Yang Jian in secret, seized them all, and threw up a palisade at Yuzhang.
